key_insight: This survey maps medical LLMs to real clinical needs by pairing a five-level competency framework with reasoning types and benchmark results across leading models.
clinical_relevance: It helps clinicians and healthcare teams see where AI is stronger today—such as diagnosis support versus dialogue and decision support—and where it still falls short for safe workflow use.
method: Defined a five-level medical competency ladder based on Miller’s Pyramid, from recall to dynamic case management.
Connected deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning patterns to common clinical goals and tasks.
Built a benchmark spanning five reasoning levels and evaluated 18 state-of-the-art models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new benchmark and comparative testing of 18 models, finding specialist medical models better on diagnosis-centric tasks while general models perform better in decision support and dialogue.
watch_item: Key limitations remain around data scarcity, hallucination, and weak grounding, which can affect reliability in real clinical settings.
paper_title: Aligning Clinical Needs and AI Capabilities: A Survey on LLMs for Medical Reasoning
